title: Sojat Pure Henna Powder — Complete Dye Release & Application Guide
shortIntro: Master the art of mixing Sojat Lawsonia Inermis henna for rich mahogany-burgundy stain and deep natural hair conditioning.
overview: Harvested from Sojat, Rajasthan — the Henna capital of India — pure Lawsonia Inermis is renowned worldwide for its high lawsone pigment density. This comprehensive guide details the exact dye release process, liquid ratios, and step-by-step application technique.
whatIsThis: 100% natural, unadulterated Lawsonia Inermis leaf powder that has been dried under shade, micro-milled and ultra-fine cloth-sifted for maximum dye yield.
keyBenefits: Rich, long-lasting mahogany reddish-brown stain on hair and skin
Natural hair coat that seals split ends and adds glossy shine
Zero synthetic chemicals, PPD, ammonia, or metallic salts
Ultra-fine cloth-sifted texture for clog-free cone or bowl mixing
ingredients: 100% Pure Lawsonia Inermis (Henna) Leaf Powder harvested from Sojat, Rajasthan
whoShouldUse: Anyone looking for a 100% natural red-brown hair dye, natural scalp conditioner, or professional Mehendi artists looking for reliable rich stain.
whoShouldAvoid: Individuals with rare G6PD deficiency should consult a medical physician before applying pure henna.
howToUse:
Step 1: Take desired powder quantity (approx 100g for shoulder hair).
Step 2: Mix with warm water and 1-2 tbsp lemon juice or tea decoction into a thick yoghurt consistency.
Step 3: Cover and let sit for 6-8 hours at room temperature for dye release.
Step 4: Apply evenly on clean dry hair. Leave for 2-3 hours before washing with plain water.
quantityPreparation: 100g for root touch-ups or short hair, 200g for shoulder length hair, 300g+ for long waist length hair.
storageInstructions: Store unused powder in a cool, dark, airtight container. Mixed paste can be frozen for up to 3 months.
importantNotes: Do not shampoo hair immediately after rinsing henna. Color deepens naturally over 24 to 48 hours via oxidation.

faqs.question: How long does Sojat Henna stain last on hair?
faqs.answer: Henna binds permanently with hair keratin. The color remains rich for 4-6 weeks with natural fading only on new hair growth.

faqs.question: Can I cover grey hair completely with Sojat Henna?
faqs.answer: Yes! Grey hair absorbs henna pigment beautifully, turning into a warm copper-red shade. For a natural black shade, follow with Natural Indigo Powder.

title: How to Use Natural Indigo Powder for Deep Black Hair
shortIntro: The ultimate 2-step natural black hair routine using pure Sojat Henna and Indigo leaf powder without synthetic chemicals.
overview: Natural Indigo (Indigofera Tinctoria) is an ancient plant leaf powder that produces a deep blue-black pigment. When applied on hair previously treated with Henna, it yields a rich, natural midnight black shade.
whatIsThis: Pure Indigofera Tinctoria leaf powder harvested, solar-dried, and finely ground without additives or metallic dyes.
keyBenefits: Provides a natural 100% chemical-free black hair shade
Eliminates grey hair when used in the 2-step Henna + Indigo method
Soothes scalp irritation and conditions hair fibers
whoShouldUse: People with grey hair or dark hair wanting a deep black or dark brown natural hair color without chemical hair dyes.
whoShouldAvoid: Do not apply Indigo alone on light or grey hair without Henna base, as it may result in a bluish-green hue.
howToUse:
Step 1: Apply Sojat Henna first and rinse with plain water.
Step 2: Mix Indigo powder with lukewarm water into a smooth paste. Apply immediately (Indigo dye releases within 10-15 minutes).
Step 3: Leave on hair for 1-2 hours, then rinse thoroughly with plain water.
quantityPreparation: Use equal parts Indigo to Henna weight (e.g. 100g Henna on Day 1, 100g Indigo on Day 2).
storageInstructions: Keep Indigo powder tightly sealed away from sunlight and moisture. Mixed Indigo paste MUST be used immediately and cannot be stored or frozen.
importantNotes: Do not use shampoo for 48 hours after Indigo application to allow full dye oxidation.

faqs.question: Why must Indigo be applied after Henna?
faqs.answer: Henna provides the orange-red base pigment (Lawsone) that allows Indigo (Indican) to bind strongly to the hair shaft, creating a dark black color.

faqs.answer: Yes! Mixing Henna and Indigo together in a single step yields warm brown to chestnut shades, whereas a 2-step process yields jet black.
